data.value: Your checking account holds 1,200 and a holiday savings account 800. With both included, Home shows 2,000; with the savings account left out, it shows 1,200.

data.name: Account_IncludeInTotalsHint
data.value: Counts in the balance on Home, in reports and budgets.

data.name: Help_AccountType_Text
data.value: The type decides how the account is shown and counted. Cash, checking, savings and credit card are money you use day to day. A loan is money you owe, money lent is money someone owes you, and an asset (for example a car or gold) has a value you update yourself. Loans, money lent and assets are kept apart from the money you can spend.

data.name: Help_AccountType_Example
data.value: A credit card with 300 spent shows −300. A car worth 9,000 is an asset and does not make your spendable balance look larger.

data.name: Help_OpeningBalance_Text
data.value: The amount in the account at the start of the chosen day, before any transaction you record for that day or later. Zanance adds your transactions to it, so the balance shown is what you recorded – it is not read from a bank.

data.name: Help_OpeningBalance_Example
data.value: Your bank shows 2,350 this morning. Enter 2,350 with today's date, then record today's purchases as transactions.

data.name: Help_OpeningUnknown_Text
data.value: Choose this if you do not know the amount yet. The account starts at zero and totals that include it are marked as incomplete, so they are never mistaken for exact numbers. You can enter the real amount later in the account.

data.name: Help_ReportCurrency_Text
data.value: Only for converted totals: amounts in other currencies are converted into this currency with the exchange rates you enter, and the date of the rates is shown. Totals per currency always stay as they are, and nothing new is created in this currency. Without a rate, the converted total is marked as incomplete.

data.name: Help_ReportCurrency_Example
data.value: Accounts in EUR and USD, valuation currency EUR: Home shows 2,000 EUR and 4,000 USD, and below them "≈ 5,680 EUR at rates of 12 Aug" once a USD rate exists.

data.name: Help_MonthStartDay_Text
data.value: Budgets, Home, reports and the transaction filters work with months. If your money arrives on a fixed day, let the month start on that day, so each month runs from one payday to the next. Plans and their due dates do not move.

data.name: Help_MonthStartDay_Example
data.value: Your salary arrives on the 25th. With the month starting on the 25th, “September” runs from 25 September to 24 October.

data.name: Help_Mode_Text
data.value: Both show the same data and calculations. Advanced shows more options directly – for example category limits, account scopes, weekly budgets and contracts. Switching back never removes anything; options already in use are summarised where they matter.

data.name: Help_AppLock_Text
data.value: Asks for your fingerprint, face or device PIN when you open Zanance and when you come back after 30 seconds. The lock hides the app; it does not encrypt the data on this device.

data.name: Help_NotificationDetails_Text
data.value: By default a reminder only says that a payment is due, so nothing private appears on the lock screen. Turn this on to see the plan's name and amount in the notification.

data.name: Help_NotificationDetails_Example
data.value: Off: “A payment is due today.” On: “Rent – 900.00 EUR today.”

data.name: Help_AmountMode_Text
data.value: Fixed: always the same amount. Estimated: about this amount, for example electricity; forecasts show it as an estimate. Unknown: no amount yet – you enter it when the payment is due, and forecasts are marked as incomplete until then.

data.name: Help_WeekendRule_Text
data.value: If a due date falls on a weekend – or, when you choose it, on a public holiday of your region – the payment can be expected on the working day before or after, as many banks do.

data.name: Help_WeekendRule_Example
data.value: Salary on the 30th, which is a Saturday: with “working day before” it is expected on Friday the 29th.

data.name: Help_AutoPost_Text
data.value: On the due date the plan's transaction is recorded for you the next time you open the app. It is marked as unreviewed, so you can check it. Without this, the payment waits under Plans until you confirm it. A payment is never recorded twice.

data.name: Help_AutoPost_Example
data.value: Rent of 900 is due on the 1st. When you open the app on the 2nd, the entry is already there, waiting for your review.

data.name: Help_PlanApplyFrom_Text
data.value: A change can apply to all payments or only from a date on. Payments before that date keep their old amount and day, so your history stays correct.

data.name: Help_PlanApplyFrom_Example
data.value: Your rent rises from 900 to 950 in March: apply from 1 March, and January and February stay at 900.

data.name: Help_Reimbursable_Text
data.value: Mark an expense that someone will pay back – for example a work trip or a dinner you paid for friends. It stays an expense until the money comes back; the repayment is recorded as a refund of it, never as income, and open amounts are listed under “Owed to me”.

data.name: Help_Reimbursable_Example
data.value: You pay 120 for a team lunch and your employer pays it back: mark the expense; when the 120 arrive, record them as its refund.

data.name: Help_ForeignAmount_Text
data.value: Keep the original amount when you paid abroad or online in another currency. The account is charged with the amount in its own currency; the original amount is shown with the entry.

data.name: Help_ForeignAmount_Example
data.value: A hotel costs 150 USD and your card is charged 139.20 EUR: amount 139.20 EUR, original 150 USD.

data.name: Help_SpendingType_Text
data.value: Used by flex budgets. Fixed: the same bill every month, such as rent. Non-monthly: bills that come a few times a year, such as insurance – they get a monthly share. Flexible: everyday spending, which shares one limit.

data.name: Help_SpendingType_Example
data.value: Car insurance of 600 a year is non-monthly: the budget sets aside 50 each month for it.

data.name: Help_BudgetMethod_Text
data.value: Limits: a maximum for the month and, if you like, per category – the simplest choice. Envelopes: you assign the money you have now to categories; the budget shows what is not assigned yet. Flex: fixed bills come from your plans, non-monthly bills get a monthly share, and one limit covers everything else.

data.name: Help_BudgetMethod_Example
data.value: Flex with rent of 900 as a plan: a yearly insurance of 600 gets 50 a month, and a flexible limit of 700 covers groceries, eating out and the rest.

data.name: Help_Rollover_Text
data.value: Decides what happens with the rest of the previous period. None: every period starts fresh. Surplus: money you did not spend is added to the new limit. Surplus and deficit: overspending is also taken from the new limit.

data.name: Help_Rollover_Example
data.value: Limit 500 and you spent 450 last month: with surplus, this month's limit is 550. Had you spent 560, “surplus and deficit” would make it 440.

data.name: Help_BudgetPeriod_Text
data.value: Besides the month you can budget per week or per two weeks – for example when you are paid every two weeks or want a weekly grocery limit. Each period has its own limits; the monthly budget stays separate. Envelopes and flex are monthly methods.

data.name: Help_BudgetPeriod_Example
data.value: A weekly limit of 120 for groceries from Monday to Sunday; next week starts again with 120, or more with rollover.

data.name: Help_FortnightStart_Text
data.value: Two-week budgets repeat every 14 days from this day. Choose a payday, so each period runs from one pay to the next.

data.name: Help_FortnightStart_Example
data.value: Paid every second Friday, last on 18 September: the periods run 18 September – 1 October, 2 – 15 October, and so on.

data.name: Help_BackupPassword_Text
data.value: The backup file is encrypted with this password (AES-256). Nobody can open it without the password – not even the developer – so keep the password somewhere safe. It is not stored in the app, and a forgotten password cannot be recovered.

data.name: Help_GoalPriority_Text
data.value: When the money set aside is not enough for all goals, goals with a higher priority are covered first. The priority changes no amount; it only decides the order in which shortfalls are shown.

data.name: Notify_OfferText
data.value: Zanance can remind you before rent, bills or your salary are due, and when a budget is almost used up. Reminders are created on this device only, and the lock screen shows no amounts unless you allow it. You can change this anytime in Settings.

data.name: Notify_OffText

data.name: About_DataText
data.value: Zanance needs no account and shows no advertising. Your financial data is kept on this device and in the backups you create, and it is not sent to the developer or to anyone else. Cloud backup is optional and uses only your own storage, once you connect it.

data.name: About_LicencesText
data.value: Zanance is built with the following software and fonts. Their licences ask for these notices.

data.name: Home_StartText

data.name: Forecast_NoPlansHint
data.value: Add your regular income and bills as plans to see how your balance develops.

data.name: Help_DefaultCurrency_Text
data.value: New accounts, goals, budgets and exchange rates start in this currency; you can change it each time. Existing accounts and entries keep their currency, and an entry is always in the currency of its account.

data.name: Help_DefaultCurrency_Example
data.value: Your accounts are in EUR and USD. With EUR here, a new account starts in EUR; your USD account stays in USD.

data.name: Settings_DefaultCurrencyHint

data.name: Help_DefaultAccount_Text
data.value: Quick add on Home, the widget and receipts use this account. The entry form always shows it, and you can pick another one for a single entry. Only cash, bank and card accounts can be the default; without one, the form asks which account to use.

data.name: Help_DefaultAccount_Example

data.name: Help_RateFreshness_Text

data.value: Some money is in your totals but is not meant for everyday payments, for example a savings account with notice or money abroad. Switch this off for such accounts: the forecast of your lowest balance then leaves them out, while every total still includes them. Zanance never decides this for you.

data.name: Help_GoalType_Text

data.value: Fixed amount: the same amount on each date. Share of income: a percentage of last month's income – only real income counts, never transfers, refunds or money moved from savings. Spending cut: spend less in one category; the budget changes only when you tap "Apply to budget".

data.name: Kpi_K01_Question
data.value: How much is left in this period's budget?

data.name: Kpi_K01_Definition
data.value: The limit plus what was carried over, minus expenses reduced by refunds.

data.name: Kpi_K01_Included
data.value: Expenses and refunds of the budget's accounts and categories|Sub-categories with their parent

data.name: Kpi_K01_Excluded
data.value: Transfers and card payments|Loan principal|Holding purchases and sales|Adjustments and opening balances|Income

data.name: Kpi_K02_Question
data.value: Will I run short before my next income?

data.name: Kpi_K02_Definition
data.value: The usable balance of today, plus planned receipts and minus planned payments of each day, minus day-to-day spending if you set an estimate. The lowest point minus protected money is the headroom – an estimate, never "safe to spend".

data.name: Kpi_K02_Included
data.value: Accounts usable for payments|Entries recorded for later days|Open plan payments, overdue ones today|Your day-to-day estimate, if set|Money set aside and marked as protected

data.name: Kpi_K02_Excluded
data.value: Budgets and monthly shares|Holdings, debts and money owed to you|Credit limits|Card purchases – only the card payment counts

data.name: Kpi_K03_Definition
data.value: What is reached divided by the target; the rest is what is still needed.

data.name: Kpi_K03_Included
data.value: A balance goal: the balance of its account|Money set aside: what is set aside and covered

data.name: Kpi_K03_Excluded
data.value: Money moved in from other accounts as income|Price changes

data.name: Kpi_K04_Question
data.value: Which payments are coming and how much are they?

data.name: Kpi_K04_Definition
data.value: What is still to pay of open plan payments due within 30 days, overdue ones included. Known, estimated (≈) and unknown amounts stay apart.

data.name: Kpi_K04_Included
data.value: Expense plans|Transfers to cards, loans or accounts kept aside|Only the outstanding part of a partly paid payment

data.name: Kpi_K04_Excluded
data.value: Settled and skipped payments|Transfers between usable accounts|Unknown amounts are counted, never added as zero

data.name: Kpi_K05_Question
data.value: Did I earn more than I spent?

data.name: Kpi_K05_Definition
data.value: Income you earned minus what you spent on consumption in the period.

data.name: Kpi_K05_Included
data.value: Income on the accounts of the scope, minus income paid back|Expenses, reduced by refunds and reimbursements|Interest and fees, counted once as expenses

data.name: Kpi_K05_Excluded
data.value: Transfers between your accounts|Card payments and loan principal|Holding purchases and sales|Adjustments and opening balances|Price and rate changes

data.name: Kpi_K06_Question
data.value: Which share of my income was left?

data.name: Kpi_K06_Definition
data.value: The surplus divided by your income. Without income it is not available – never 0 %.

data.name: Kpi_K06_Excluded
data.value: Not a measure of wealth change, price growth or money moved to savings

data.name: Kpi_K07_Question
data.value: How many months could I cover essential costs with the money I can use?

data.name: Kpi_K07_Definition
data.value: Usable money divided by the median essential spending of the last three complete months, plus monthly shares of essential non-monthly bills.

data.name: Kpi_K07_Included

data.name: Kpi_K07_Excluded

data.name: Kpi_K08_Question

data.value: The expected amounts of active expense plans in the next 12 months: fixed, non-monthly and estimated. A monthly share is a share, not money set aside.

data.name: Kpi_K08_Excluded
data.value: Unknown amounts (counted apart)|Ended plans and skipped payments|Income plans

data.name: Kpi_K09_Question
data.value: Which part of my income goes to loan installments?

data.name: Kpi_K09_Definition

data.name: Kpi_K09_Included

data.name: Kpi_K10_Question

data.name: Kpi_K10_Excluded

data.name: Kpi_K11_Definition
data.value: Spending per category now against the previous period. While a period runs, the same number of days is compared.

data.name: Kpi_K12_Question

data.name: Help_SafetyCopy_Text
data.value: Before a backup replaces your data, Zanance keeps a safety copy of the current data on this device, so nothing is lost if the restore fails. The safety copy is not encrypted; it stays in the app's private storage and only the newest copies are kept. A backup file you create yourself is always encrypted with your password.

data.name: About_FilesBackup
data.value: Everything you entered: accounts, entries, plans, budgets, rates, goals, holdings with their events and prices, forecast snapshots, display units and the Home layout. It is encrypted with your password. Device preferences (theme, language, digits, reminders) are not included.

data.name: About_FilesCsv
data.value: Your entries, and your holdings in a file of their own, for a spreadsheet. A CSV export is not a backup: plans, budgets, goals and snapshots are not in it.

data.name: About_FilesPdf
data.value: The report you chose, with its period, currency and the accounts it covers on the page. It is for reading and sharing; it cannot be restored.

data.name: About_PlatformsText

data.name: About_ProblemText
